 COMMON JUDGMENT

The Petitioners have filed these petitions under Sec.166 of Indian Motor Vehicle Act seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by them in a road accident dated  3 MVC No.7680 & 7681/2018  SCCH-24 26.06.2018.

Both the petitions have arisen out of a common accident, therefore both the petitions are clubbed together as per order dated 22.01.2020 and common evidence is lead and common judgment is passed.
 2.

cautions and slow manner by following all traffic rules in order to go to their regular job, when they reached opposite to Colombia Asia Hospital, next to dry garbage waste station by that time driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA 02MK6278 came from back side in a high speed, rash and negligent manner, unmindfully without observing the Smt.Swetha N vs Dr.Chethan Nagaraj on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15992911/
2 movements of other vehicle and dashed against their vehicle, due to impact both sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately they were rushed to Columbia Asia Hospital,
Bangalore, wherein admitted as an inpatient for one week  4 MVC No.7680 & 7681/2018  SCCH-24 and underwent surgery and discharged with an advise.

So far they have spent Rs.1,60,000/ and Rs.1,20,000/
towards medical and other expenses.
She is advised to go for another operation in the near future days for removal of implants.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The Petitioners have filed these petitions under Sec.166 of Indian Motor Vehicle Act seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by them in a road accident dated  3 MVC No.7680 & 7681/2018  SCCH-24 26.06.2018.
Therefore, the Respondents being the R.C owner and insurer of the offending vehicle are liable to pay the compensation to them.
Further submitted that the accident was occurred due to negligence on the part of the petitioner and there was no negligence on his part.
Further submitted that the vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA02MK6278 is not at all involved in the accident.
The first respondent had been willfully entrusted his vehicle to a person who did not possess valid and effective driving license to drive the same as on the date of accident which is clear breach of terms and conditions of the policy.
Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petitions against them.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The Respondents have not obtained any contrary admissions from the mouth of the PWs.1 and 2 to support their defence.
As such, there are no reasons to discard the evidence of PWs.1 and 2 and documents produced by them and accept the version of the Respondents.
Further, the wound certificates produced by the Petitioners as per Exs.P.7 and P.14 clearly disclose that, on account of accident the Petitioners have sustained grievous injuries.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation from the Respondents.
But, to substantiate this, the Petitioner has not examined her employer and she has also not produced vouchers or the bank statement to ascertain her income.
Therefore, the version of the Petitioner that she was earning a sum of Rs.20,000/ per month is not acceptable.
At the time of accident the Petitioner was aged about 31 years as could be make out from Ex.P.12/Aadhar card wherein her birth date shown as 26.02.1987.
The accident took place in the year 2018.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.1,31,221/ under the head of Medical Expenses.
After the accident, the Petitioner was treated in the said above hospital for a period of nearly 3 days.
Hence, she is entitled for a sum of Rs.12,500/ under this head.
Therefore, as on the date of the accident the Petitioner's age is considered as 31 years.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled a sum of Rs.1,20,000/
(Rs.12,500/ x 12 x 16 x 5%= Rs.1,20,000/) under this head.
The Petitioner was aged about 31 years at the time of accident.
She has sustained grievous injuries as discussed above, as per consideration of this Tribunal, she is suffering from 5% permanent disability.
The Petitioner has to suffer this disability throughout her life.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.78,077/ under the head of Medical Expenses.
After the accident, the Petitioner was treated in the said above hospital for a period of nearly 3 days.
Therefore, considering the nature of injuries and the duration of treatment it can be said that the Petitioner has required at least one month time for recovering of the  27 MVC No.7680 & 7681/2018  SCCH-24 injuries sustained by him.
The Petitioner was aged about 41 years at the time of accident.
Therefore, the respondents being the RC owner and insurer are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
However, as the policy is existed and hence the respondent No.2 insurer is directed to indemnify the respondent No.1/owner and to deposit the compensation.
